ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Mild early gastrointestinal symptoms

A 25-year-old woman returns 5 days after starting sertraline. She has mild nausea and two loose stools daily but maintains oral intake. Temperature, pulse and neurologic examination are normal, with no clonus or rigidity. Which explanation best fits this presentation?

  1. Acute paralytic ileus from muscarinic blockade
  2. Withdrawal from sertraline
  3. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
  4. Common gastrointestinal effects of an SSRI
  5. Serotonin syndrome requiring clonus to be ignored
Answer and explanation

Common gastrointestinal effects of an SSRI

Isolated mild gastrointestinal symptoms can occur early; they do not by themselves establish serotonin syndrome.

Option explanations

Common gastrointestinal effects of an SSRI: Isolated mild gastrointestinal symptoms can occur early; they do not by themselves establish serotonin syndrome.

Serotonin syndrome requiring clonus to be ignored: The case lacks the mental, autonomic and neuromuscular pattern supporting that diagnosis.

Acute paralytic ileus from muscarinic blockade: Ileus causes reduced bowel activity and distension, not this pattern.

Withdrawal from sertraline: She has just started treatment and has not stopped taking it.

Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: There is no dopamine-blocking exposure, hyperthermia or severe rigidity.
